text: Embun is a Rust UI toolkit with glass controls that match macOS 27. You describe the UI as a tree of elements, Embun lays it out and draws it with wgpu, and your app gets a message when the user presses something.

heading: Install
text: Embun draws with wgpu, so it needs Metal (macOS), Vulkan, DirectX 12 or OpenGL. The tests run on macOS with Metal and on Linux with Vulkan and OpenGL. Windows is untested.

heading: Your first app
text: An app is a struct, a message type and two functions. update changes the struct when a message arrives. view returns the elements for the current state. This one is a counter with two buttons.

heading: How a press becomes a change
text: Your app owns all the state. Controls such as switch, slider and text_input take their value from you and send a message when it should change.

heading: Styling
text: Elements are styled with methods named after Tailwind classes: gap_3, p_5, rounded_full, items_center. Colors come from the Theme that view receives, so your UI follows light and dark mode.

Embun lays elements out with flexbox, through taffy. row places children left to right, and column (or div) stacks them top to bottom. Sizes are in logical pixels, and spacing methods count in steps of 4 px: p_3 is 12 px of padding, gap_2 is 8 px.

heading: Rows and columns
text: Put rows in columns and columns in rows. gap_* spaces the children, p_*, px_* and py_* pad them, and items_* and justify_* align them across and along the direction.

heading: Growing and fixed sizes
text: w, h and size set pixels, w_full and h_full fill the parent, and grow takes the space left over. spacer() is an empty element that grows, which pushes siblings apart.

heading: Wrapping
text: flex_wrap on a row moves children that do not fit onto the next line.

heading: Absolute positioning
text: absolute takes an element out of the flow and places it from its parent's edges with top, right, bottom and left. inset(0.0) stretches it over the whole parent.

heading: Scrolling
text: scroll_y makes a container scroll vertically when its children are taller than it. For long lists use list, which builds only the visible rows.

heading: Surfaces and borders
text: bg fills with a color, rounded and the rounded_* sizes round the corners, and border draws an outline. Take colors from the theme so they follow light and dark mode.

heading: Gradients
text: bg_gradient(top, bottom) blends two colors from top to bottom.

Text is set in Inter, which is embedded in the library, so it measures the same on every machine. Embun does not use Apple's fonts. Set Settings::system_fonts(true) to also load installed fonts, which you need for emoji and for scripts Inter does not cover.

heading: Size, weight and color
text: text_xs up to text_4xl set common sizes, and text_size takes any size in pixels. font_medium, font_semibold and font_bold set the weight. Size, weight and color are inherited, so set them on a parent to style everything inside it.

heading: Wrapping and alignment
text: Text wraps at the width of its box. text_center and text_right align the lines, and leading sets the line height as a multiple of the font size.

heading: One line
text: no_wrap keeps text on one line however narrow its box is, and clip on the box cuts what does not fit. Together they make the single-line cells a table needs.

heading: Images
text: Image::from_rgba takes raw pixels. Image::open and Image::from_bytes read PNG and JPEG, and return an ImageError that names the file and the problem. Set w or h to scale an image, and rounded to clip its corners. When you set only one of them, the aspect ratio is kept.

Buttons are glass. They frost whatever is behind them, so they look right over a photo, a gradient or your own content, and they are less useful over a flat color. Every example on this site is drawn by Embun's own renderer.

heading: Button
text: button takes a label. on_press sets the message to send. prominent tints it with the accent color for the main action in a view.

heading: Sizes
text: ControlSize has four sizes: Small, Regular (the default), Large and ExtraLarge. Their heights follow the buttons in macOS 27.0.1.

heading: Icon buttons
text: An icon button is round and shows a glyph. Give it a label, because a screen reader has nothing else to read out.

heading: Toolbar
text: toolbar_group joins its items into one glass pill, the way macOS groups back and forward. Put other buttons beside it.

heading: Sidebar
text: sidebar is a glass panel with a heading and rows. Pass true to sidebar_item for the selected row. Give each row a key so Embun keeps its hover and press state when the list changes.
These controls hold no state of their own. You pass the current value and a message, and your update changes the value. All of them tell screen readers their role and state.

heading: Switch
text: switch(theme, on, message). The knob slides when the value changes. Give it a label so a screen reader can say what it turns on.

heading: Checkbox
text: checkbox(theme, label, checked, message) draws the label beside the box, and pressing the label toggles it too.

heading: Radio
text: radio(theme, label, selected, message). Build a group by calling it once per option, with selected true for the current one, and give each a key.

heading: Slider
text: slider(theme, value, on_change) takes a value from 0 to 1 and calls on_change with the new one while the user drags. It also responds to the arrow keys, Home and End when focused, and screen readers can increment, decrement or set it.

heading: Segmented control
text: segmented(theme, options, selected, on_select) shows one of a few options at a time. It sizes itself to its labels. With a segment focused, Left and Right select the neighbouring one.

heading: Dropdown
text: dropdown(theme, options, selected, open, on_open, on_select) is a pop-up picker: a glass button that shows the selected option and opens a menu of all of them. Your app owns selected and open. on_open(true) is sent when the button is pressed, and on_open(false) when it is pressed again, when Escape is pressed, or when the user presses anywhere outside the menu. A press that closes the menu does nothing else, as on macOS. Up and Down move between the options once one has focus.

heading: Disclosure
text: disclosure(theme, title, open, on_toggle, content) shows or hides its content when the heading is pressed. While it is closed the content is not in the tree at all. The heading tells screen readers whether the group is expanded or collapsed.
Feedback pieces that tell the user something is happening, how much, or what a control does.

heading: Progress bar
text: progress(theme, value) takes a value from 0 to 1 and clamps anything else. It is 200 px wide and 6 px tall unless you set w. Screen readers get the value, and a name when you call label.

heading: When you cannot say how long
text: progress_indeterminate sweeps a segment back and forth along the bar, and spinner shows three dots that hop one after another. Both keep the window redrawing while they are on screen, and stop when you remove them. Give each a label such as "Loading", because there is no value to read out.

heading: Badge
text: badge(theme, label) is a small accent-colored pill for a count. It is 18 px tall and grows with its label. Use .bg(...) for another color.

heading: Divider
text: divider(theme) is a 1 px line across its parent, and vertical_divider(theme) runs down it.

heading: Tooltip
text: tooltip(text) on any element, or on a button, shows a small box near the pointer after it has rested there for about half a second. It also appears when the pointer rests on anything inside the element. Moving off, pressing or leaving the window hides it. Tooltips are not shown for keyboard focus yet.

table(theme, columns, rows, cell) is a header row over a list of rows. Only the rows on screen are built, so a million rows cost the same as ten and scroll as fast as a list. Your app owns the data, the sort order and the selection.

heading: Columns
text: A Column is a title and a width. Column::new shares the leftover width equally with the other growing columns, grow(2.0) takes two parts instead of one, and width(110.0) fixes it in pixels. right() aligns the title and the cells to the right, for numbers.

heading: Cells
text: cell(row, column) builds one cell, and can return any element. For text, return text(...).no_wrap(): the text stays on one line and is cut at the column edge instead of wrapping into the next row. Element::clip does the same cutting for anything else.

heading: What is not there yet
text: Columns cannot be resized by dragging, rows cannot be selected in groups, and Tab walks through every built row instead of stopping once on the table. Screen readers see the table, its rows, cells and headers and which row is selected, but not the row and column counts.
Text fields show the value your app owns. When the user types, Embun calls the function you passed and sends your update the new text. You store it, and the next view passes it back in.

heading: Single line
text: text_input(value, on_change) is 28 px tall and 200 px wide until you set w, h or grow. placeholder shows hint text while the field is empty, and label gives it a name for screen readers, since a placeholder is not a label.

heading: Multiple lines
text: text_area works the same way. Return starts a new line, long lines wrap at the width of the field, Up and Down move between lines, the wheel scrolls it, and the view follows the caret.

heading: What the user can do
text: Double-click to select a word is not built yet. The cursor moves by character, so an emoji made of several characters takes several presses.

list(count, row_height, row) is a scrolling list that builds and lays out only the rows on screen. A million rows of 32 px scroll at about 0.12 ms per step on an Apple M5, because the other 999,980 rows are never built.

heading: Responding to a press
text: Put on_press on the row you return. The message can carry the index, so your update knows which row was pressed.
Menus and dialogs are overlays: layers over the whole window that frost the finished frame beneath them. A menu over a toolbar shows the toolbar through its glass.

heading: Menu
text: menu is a glass panel of rows. menu_item is a plain row, menu_check_item adds a check mark column so labels line up whether checked or not, and menu_separator draws a thin line between groups.

heading: Showing a menu
text: Wrap it in popover(dismiss, content) and place it with absolute, top and left, for example just under the button that opens it. Clicking outside, or pressing Escape, sends dismiss, and your update should then stop showing it. With a menu item focused, Up and Down move to the neighbouring item.

heading: Dialog
text: dialog(dismiss, content) dims the window and centers its content, usually a dialog_panel. Clicking the dimmed area or pressing Escape sends dismiss. The panel is solid, not glass, so the glass buttons on it have something to frost. Pressing the panel itself does not close the dialog.
view receives a Theme. Take colors from it and your UI follows light and dark mode, Reduce Transparency, and whether the window has focus.

heading: Colors
text: background, surface, label, secondary_label, separator, accent and on_accent change with the appearance. For a color of your own, theme.pick(light, dark) returns the first value in light mode and the second in dark mode.

heading: Window settings
text: Settings chooses the window's size and starting look. By default everything follows the system.

heading: Glass without focus
text: As on macOS, glass in a window that has lost focus is frosted more, and prominent buttons lose their color. theme.focused tells you which state you are in.

heading: Accessibility
text: Every element is in the accessibility tree that AccessKit hands to VoiceOver, Narrator and Orca, with its role, name and bounds. Buttons can be pressed and text fields edited from the screen reader, and keyboard focus is shared with it. Tab and Shift-Tab move focus between controls, and Space or Return presses the focused one.
